column1: # Yoshi and the Mysterious Book (Switch 2, update 1.0.2, v131072). In bring-up: reaches its title screen and opening on the Mac; 133,154 shaders, some not translated yet (README.md)

# Unreal Engine 5.4.4 (SDK MW+EpicGames+UnrealEngine-5_4_4 in main; its NVN2 RHI), SDK 20.5.15 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce). Modules main + subsdk2 (movie) + sdk. subsdk0 (DLSS) and subsdk1 (CUDA) are not loaded: main imports nothing from them.
# Packed from a NUP container (scripts/pack_nup.py), no base game: the update's RomFS holds every path of its base. One IoStore container, PJ045-Sage.utoc / .ucas, beside one pak.
# v131072 is the update's title version; the NUP carries no NACP, 1.0.2 is what the title screen shows

# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure, not measured here). The NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on; the rewriter gives Unreal's engine region what the alias region has room for (dm/tools/ue_region.py) and cuts its allocator (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py, layout UE 5).
# 256 MB in front + 16 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + heap region: Splatoon Raiders' split as a starting point, to be measured

# No shader library: the global shaders are in the pak's GlobalShaderCache-SP_GLSL_SAGE.bin, the others inline in the cooked packages of the IoStore container, each Oodle-compressed (uepak.py resource_maps).
# Unreal combines vertex and pixel shaders per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs)
